name: E01 | Lester’s Pager Panic
topic: Dual modular filter + per-row stream permutation
summary: Keep rows satisfying BOTH (col_A*col_B) mod col_C == 7 AND (col_A+col_B) mod col_C == (col_D mod col_C). For each genuine row, base-41 decode then invert the per-row alphabet permutation idx -> (k*idx+m) mod 41 with k = 1+(col_A mod 40), m = col_D mod 41 (use pow(k,-1,41)). Sort genuine rows by (col_C mod 5 asc, col_D mod 2 asc, -col_E desc, packet_id asc). Concatenate decodes, strip the fixed 2-byte marker \x1b\x13. Decoys satisfy only one condition (one decodes to a fake flag); using a single filter yields garbage.

name: E02 | Vinewood Shift Change
summary: Keep the row where SHA1(timestamp) ends in a3 AND SHA256(route) starts with nibble 4. Undo a columnar transposition of width 9, then affine-decrypt with a=7,b=11. The sample is affine(transpose(english),7,11), 441 = 9x49; naive frequency analysis returns a wrong pair (1,20). Ignore the Caesar-5 decoy (FTA{wrong_route}) and the single-stage affine decoy (a near-miss flag).

name: E03 | Sandy Shores Hidden Stash
summary: Carve the three deleted inodes; the genuine one is /ledger.dat whose sealed byte length equals the span= field on activity.log line 42. Build an 8-byte repeating XOR key arithmetically from that same line's host + relay fields; unmask, then invert the pipeline base64 -> byte-reverse -> zlib (i.e. zlib-decompress, reverse, base64-decode). Decoys /ledger.bak and /notes.tmp decode to bait flags.

name: E04 | Del Perro Camera Roll
summary: Parse the watermark metadata to recover the gate coefficients + salt; select pixels satisfying (3x+5y) mod 7 == 4; read bits 2..3 of R,G,B column-major; XOR with the repeating 32-byte SHA256 key; then parse a 2-byte big-endian length + gzip(utf-7(flag)). Decoys: a metadata 'flag' and a naive 2-LSB bait stream.

name: E05 | Wrong Extension, Right Exit
summary: Treat impound_dossier.pdf as a PDF+GIF89a+ZIP polyglot. AES-128 key = PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(password = SERIAL + '|' + ROUTE_CODE, salt, 50000, dklen=16), where SERIAL is the AcroForm field 'serial' (not the body text) and ROUTE_CODE is printed in the visible body; the IV rides in the ZIP extra field. Decrypt to vault.db (tables operators/routes/seals joined on a TEXT token); the flag is the XOR of the three joined *_hex columns. Decoys: a fake flag row and a grep-able fake 'ARCHIVE KEY' comment.

name: M01 | Fleeca Vault Glitch
topic: Two-stage stored injection + DB-keyed hashing + session gate
summary: register (safe) -> sync (stores a derived alias) -> load (interpolates the stored alias raw). Bypass the custom scrubber with a /*...*/ comment (it strips -- and ; but not /* */) to run a second-order UNION injection against the escrow table advertised in config.core_ledger. Authenticate with trunc(sha256('fleeca-h2'|per_user_salt|pw|user[::-1]|server_pepper))[:20] using salt+pepper read from fleeca.db, and present a valid token = HMAC(secret_key, user|nonce). Decoys: honeypot admin/sunshine and a fake vault table.

name: M02 | Airport Ghost Flight
topic: Nested frames + scoped seal + sequence-keyed mask
summary: Parse the classic pcap. Outer frame: magic 0xDEAD1A70 LE, type 0x0A, seal = CRC32(frame[0:12] || payload) SKIPPING the 2-byte route field. Inner frame: magic 0x1A70C0DE LE, ver==1, itype 0x5C. XOR the inner data with an LCG keystream keyed by the inner sequence, then order by the inner seq (ignore the outer seq). Decoys: a naive-whole-frame-CRC group reassembling to a fake flag, plus bad-seal / wrong-type frames.

name: M03 | LSPD Midnight Audit
topic: Keyed hash chain + block checkpoints + nested delta
summary: Verify chain_i = HMAC-SHA256(prev_chain || entry_data, salt) with the salt recovered from the log header/CHAIN_SPEC, and verify per-block checkpoint roots (every 100 entries). Locate the three forged entries at the chain/root breaks. Decode audit_delta.bin as nested RLE + index-derived XOR and apply it to repair. Derive the flag by selecting entries whose code ends '_ACCEPT' AND whose third field hashes into a given class, then combining the specified column per CHAIN_SPEC. Decoys: forged lines that pass an unkeyed chain, plus a decoy event sequence yielding a fake flag.

name: M04 | Underground XOR Radio
topic: Interleaved LFSRs + partial KPA + lane transpose
summary: From the exposed leading bytes of keystream_sample.bin, de-multiplex even/odd byte lanes and run Berlekamp-Massey on each lane: recover a degree-23 LFSR (taps 23,5) and a degree-17 LFSR (taps 17,3), regenerate the full keystream, invert the fixed 8-byte lane transpose, then XOR against radio_packet.bin. SIGNAL_SPEC.txt lists wrong taps/seeds and a decoy flag fragment.

name: M05 | Debugging the Dispatch
topic: Two-structure race + dual-bug stage 2 + final wrap
summary: Serialise the entire critical section (the per-lane tally dict AND the running ledger), so the seal is consistent; the fixed dispatcher emits base85(zlib(json)) containing stage2.py. Fix both stage-2 bugs — the fixed-width 32-bit rotate missing its & 0xFFFFFFFF, and the length-prefixed record parsed big-endian at offset 2 rather than little-endian at offset 3 — then undo the final base64 + rotating-XOR wrap. Decoys: a partial fix yields ARCHIVED_VALUE, and the notes carry a fake flag.

name: H01 | Zancudo Deadbolt
topic: Anti-analysis traps + chained VMs + runtime-keyed vault
summary: Defeat four independent anti-debug gates (ptrace, /proc/self/status TracerPid, a timing probe, and a parent-process-name check) — any trip diverts to a fake success path that emits a WRONG flag. VM1's result XOR-masks VM2's bytecode. The vault (need/SBOX/K/TARGET/checksum/mix) is XOR-encrypted in .rodata and decrypted at runtime with an xorshift64 keystream seeded by splitmix64(C, argv length, env byte, v1, v2). The layered check is: length gate -> FNV-1a checksum -> (SBOX[in[i]]*K[i]) mod 251 -> HMAC-like hmix. The passphrase is the flag.

name: H02 | The Recursive Freeway
summary: The junctions form a 4-regular weighted network; a topological induced-subgraph search finds 5 matches (4 near-miss decoys differing by one edge/weight). Narrow to the unique district whose weighted normalised Laplacian spectrum matches the blueprint's (rounded), then order the district's node labels by descending weighted eigenvector centrality (Perron-positive sign convention) and assemble the flag per PROTOCOL.md.

name: H03 | Impound Evidence Matryoshka
summary: Gated PNG LSB (stride/offset from the note's frequency table) -> AES-256-CTR (PBKDF2 key from the metadata-derived passphrase) -> password-gated ZIP in the trailing bytes (password = the badge recovered at layer 2) -> AES-256-GCM (nonce = SHA256('gcm'||TAG)[:12], TAG from layer 1) -> MTX-1 matrix code -> Huffman decode using the frequency table from the note -> run the recovered Python stage, which deterministically prints the flag. Decoys: PngInfo 'flag', EXIF description, trailing-bytes tag, and a ZIP bait file, each a fake flag.

name: H04 | LEGAL RAGGING
topic: Blinded RSA-CRT fault + timing oracle + freshness gate
summary: Call sign_debug on a fixed message to collect a correct and a faulty signature; un-blind each (sig_blind * r^-1 mod n) first. Faults land in p or q, so gcd(bad^e - m mod n, n) may return either prime — accept both and check p*q == n. Recover d, derive the live audit nonce one byte at a time via the verify_debug timing oracle, assemble ADMIN_MESSAGE with that nonce + a fresh timestamp, sign it as role 'admin', and submit to read the flag from the FTA_H04_FLAG environment variable. Decoys: a legacy signed token that verifies but is refused, and wrong leads in AUDIT_BRIEF.txt.

name: H05 | Last Ride Out
summary: Parse the TLV transcript: shares A/B are bound (32B element + 16B tag = 48B) while C/D are reduced (bare 32B) and re-advertised. The agreement value is Y = XA^5 * XB^11 * XC^13 * XD^17 mod p; the key is K = HKDF(salt, Y, info||sid). Choose an attacker-known target and solve for the injected C share XC = (Y* * R^-1)^(13^-1 mod (p-1)). Confirm against record 0x0020 (0x0021/0x0022 are decoys), then AES-256-GCM decrypt final_payload.enc and finally AES-256-CBC the inner blob.
